web_title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Stage 4 Markdown & Failed Support
question: What do EQT's 1W, 1D, and 4H charts and options structure show after breaking below $50 support?

epigraph.quote: Never buy a stock in Stage 4, no matter how cheap it looks on trailing earnings. Wait until the downtrend ends and buyers prove control.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein, Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets

web_blocks.title: Breakdown into Stage 4 Markdown across weekly and daily charts

web_blocks.html: Whatever EQT's geological merits, the November 20, 2026 tape confirms a clear breakdown [23]. EQT closed at $48.89, down 0.83% on the day, 7.42% over five sessions, and 10.57% over one month [23]. Price now sits 28.36% below its $68.24 high and just 1.99% above its $47.94 52-week low [23]. Every major moving average acts as overhead resistance: 10-week EMA ($52.12), 50-day SMA ($52.22), 30-week SMA ($53.13), and 200-day SMA ($55.34) [23]. Both our facts ledger (stage 4) and TradingView snapshot classify EQT as STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) [23].

web_blocks.title: Multi-timeframe 1W, 1D, and 4H momentum and volume ledger

web_blocks.html: Checking all three timeframes prevents mistaking a weak bounce for institutional buying [23]. On the weekly chart, 1W RSI dropped to 42.02 below a falling 30-week SMA ($53.13) [23]. On the daily chart, EQT sits 2.03 ATRs below its falling 50-day SMA ($52.22) with 1D RSI at 36.49 [23]. The stock also logged 8 distribution days over the past 25 sessions [23]. On the 4-hour chart, price stays below the 4H 20-EMA ($51.02) and 4H 50-SMA ($52.99) with 4H RSI at 32.66 and no upward turn [23]. Daily volume of 7.71M shares (0.90x 30-day average) signals steady selling rather than a capitulation bottom [23].

web_blocks.title: Source reconciliation, TradingView chart, and screen overrides

web_blocks.html: Full transparency requires flagging minor feed differences across our automated tools. Both market facts and TradingView agree on Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED). However, facts logs a 5-day drop of 7.42% on 0.81x 20-day volume, while TradingView prints 6.68% on 0.90x 30-day volume [23]. TheWrap dashboard labels EQT Integrated Oil with null industry breadth fields [23]. The snapshot screen also prints a stale $51.34–$53.00 band (stop $51.40) and an Attractive GARP label [23]. We override both screen tags because price broke $49.94 and 2027 attributable FCF yields only 4.58% to 5.13% [23, 29, 38].

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 showed why EQT's valuation no longer offers a margin of safety at $2.88 gas, Chapter 8 delivers the same message straight from the price chart. Between November 13 and November 20, 2026, EQT dropped 7.42% on the five-day ledger to close at $48.89—breaking right through Pivot S1 at $49.94 and sinking within two percent of its $47.94 52-week low [23].

Look at the weekly structure first, because weekly charts filter out daily noise. Stan Weinstein's 30-week moving average—the boundary line between healthy accumulation and sustained distribution—sits up at $53.13, while the 10-week EMA sits at $52.12 and the 200-day SMA hovers at $55.34 [23]. Trading 7.98% below the 30-week average and 11.65% below the 200-day average places EQT squarely inside Stage 4 Markdown in both our market-facts ledger and TradingView snapshot [23].

Check the daily and four-hour timeframes before assuming the drop is finished. Daily RSI sits at 36.49 and four-hour RSI at 32.66—oversold, yes, yet still below the 4H 20-EMA ($51.02) and 4H 50-SMA ($52.99) with no upward turn [23]. Over the past 25 trading days, EQT logged eight distribution sessions while volume on Friday's decline ran at 7.71 million shares (0.90x the 30-day average) [23]. That is steady institutional selling, not a washed-out bottom.

Macro breadth reinforces caution. The S&P 500 itself is in a Downtrend with ten distribution days in 25 sessions and just 38.8% of tracked stocks above their 50-day moving averages [23]. Meanwhile, our options desk flags NO_OPTIONS_EDGE because buying calls beneath declining 50-day and 200-day averages in a non-compounder cyclical violates risk-reward rules. Wait for Chapter 9 to see how this broken tape combines with our $50.00 Base Case fair value to force a decisive verdict.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When Pivot S1 ($49.94) breaks and price falls 2.03 ATRs below a falling 50-day average on ten market distribution days, trying to catch the bounce is not value investing—it is fighting institutional supply.

book_subsections.title: Why Even a Stage-4 Reclaim Fails the Risk-Reward Hurdle
paragraphs: Many disciplined traders ask a fair question when a quality operator drops into Stage 4: why not set a WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT trigger to buy only once EQT reclaims its 30-week ($53.13) and 200-day ($55.34) averages? Let us test that idea strictly with arithmetic. A structural Stage 2 reclaim requires buying around $53.25 to $55.50 with a protective stop near $50.00.

Compare that $55.50 reclaim entry against our Pass 2 Base Case fair value of $50.00 per share. Buying at $53.25 to $55.50 when Base Case fair value sits at $50.00 produces a negative expected return (-9.9% from $55.50 to $50.00) and fails the 1.50-to-1 reward-to-risk gate completely. Even Pivot S2 ($44.49) sits above our $39.67 EIA strip valuation and yields just 0.48-to-1 against a $33.00 structural stop (and 0.41-to-1 above our $31.22 Bear Case). Only a below-strip reset into $36.00–$38.00 ($33.00 stop) restores potential mathematical asymmetry once gas and Stage 1/2 structure recover.

book_subsections.title: Short Float, Merger Arbitrage & Options Desk Audit
paragraphs: Look at ownership and short interest under the surface. Institutional ownership remains high at 97.54%, while short interest sits at 24.35 million shares—3.93% of float, or 3.10 days to cover [24]. Part of that short float reflects merger arbitrageurs shorting EQT against long Range Resources positions, which creates mechanical supply until HSR antitrust review concludes [26, 36].

On the derivatives side, public options checks confirm NO_OPTIONS_EDGE: implied volatility and negative multi-timeframe trend structure eliminate positive call convexity below $55.34. When equity trend, normalized cash yield, and options convexity all point away from buying, disciplined capital stands completely aside.

book_subsections.title: Reading Moving Averages, Volume Dry-Up, and Macro Breadth Together
paragraphs: Notice how moving averages act as an honest institutional scoreboard. When pension funds and long-only energy desks are accumulating shares, a stock rides above rising 10-week and 30-week averages and expands on up-week volume. Today, EQT trades 6.38% below its falling 50-day average ($52.22), 7.98% below its 30-week average ($53.13), and 11.65% below its 200-day average ($55.34) [23].

Add the market regime backdrop. When the S&P 500 carries ten distribution days in 25 sessions and fewer than 40% of stocks hold their 50-day lines, catching falling knives below Pivot S1 ($49.94) destroys capital quickly [23]. Let EQT prove a multi-week Stage 1 base and a genuine Stage 2 volume breakout before putting it back on your buy screen.
